The Polymarket (CRYPTO: POL) crowd is leaning heavily bearish for the Aug. 31 trading session. The "S&P 500 (SPX) Up or Down on August 31?" contract currently reflects a 36% chance of a higher open.

Polymarket odds for S&P 500 opening on Aug. 31.
Why That Number Matters

Traders are confronting a resurgence of Middle East violence alongside crucial incoming economic indicators and corporate earnings:

Despite the escalating conflict in the Middle East and rising bond yields worldwide, the global bull market in stocks is pressing on. title: Bitcoin price holds at $78,000 as ‘digital gold’ narrative faces fresh test
detail:
Bitcoin price holds at $78,000 as ‘digital gold’ narrative faces fresh test
Simon Mugo
Sat, August 29, 2026 at 4:49 AM CDT 2 min read
BTC-USD
GC=F
^NDX
NDX
GC
Trade BTC on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Investing.com -- Bitcoin traded at $78,000 on Saturday after a sharp pullback from this week's three-month highs, testing renewed claims that the cryptocurrency is increasingly trading like gold rather than a high-beta technology asset.

Bitcoin was trading at $78,062 as of 17:10 ET, up about 0.9% over the latest session, after touching above $81,000 earlier in the week.

The pause comes as Grayscale data showed Bitcoin's 90-day correlation with gold has climbed above 50%, from barely above zero at the start of 2026.

At the same time, its correlation with the Nasdaq 100 has fallen to roughly 33% from above 60%, suggesting investors may increasingly be treating Bitcoin as a scarce monetary asset rather than a proxy for technology stocks.

The shift has coincided with renewed concern about U.S. fiscal policy after federal debt surpassed $40 trillion. Rising borrowing requirements and Treasury bond buybacks have revived the so-called debasement trade, which favors scarce assets such as gold and Bitcoin.

On-chain activity also offers little evidence of widespread selling by Bitcoin's oldest holders.

Six wallets dormant since between 2011 and 2014 moved 553.59 BTC, worth roughly $40 million, between Aug. 16 and Aug. 26, according to Galaxy Research data cited by CoinDesk.

Five sent their coins to addresses without known exchange links, while only one transferred 40 BTC to Boerse Stuttgart Digital. Galaxy said dormant Bitcoin activity during the second quarter fell to its lowest since 2022, with 2026 on course for less than half last year's total.

Long-term price optimism remains strong. Coinbase (NASDAQ:COIN) CEO Brian Armstrong recently said Bitcoin has a "good chance" of reaching $100,000 by year-end, while Binance founder Changpeng Zhao has argued Bitcoin could eventually overtake gold's market capitalization.

Yet another long-term issue is attracting attention: quantum computing.

Ripple has outlined a four-stage plan to prepare the XRP Ledger for quantum-resistant cryptography, while Bitcoin and Ethereum developers are also working on migration strategies before sufficiently advanced quantum computers could threaten existing digital signatures.

For Bitcoin, the latest pullback leaves investors weighing stronger store-of-value characteristics against persistent volatility and emerging technological risks.

Broader crypto prices were trading lower on Saturday, with most cryptos booking losses.

World no.2 crypto Ether gained 0.9% to trade at $2,450.49.

title: Bitcoin Price is Moving Like Gold, and Grayscale Says It's No Coincidence
detail:
Bitcoin Price is Moving Like Gold, and Grayscale Says It's No Coincidence
Luis Blanco
Fri, August 28, 2026 at 2:50 PM CDT 3 min read
BTC-USD
GC=F
^NDX
Trade BTC on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Grayscale's research arm warned this week that Bitcoin's correlation with gold has climbed above 50%, a shift the asset manager frames as the return of the debasement trade.

The finding marks a sharp reversal from recent years, when Bitcoin frequently traded in step with growth stocks rather than hard assets.

How Grayscale Measured Bitcoin's Shift Toward Gold

In a recent note, Grayscale Head of Research Zach Pandl reported that Bitcoin's 90-day correlation with gold rose from near zero at the start of the year to above 50%. Over the same period, its correlation with the Nasdaq 100 slipped from more than 60% to roughly 33%.

Pandl said the shift may reflect renewed investor focus on Bitcoin's scarcity, monetary independence, and role as a store of value, according to Grayscale's ongoing research series. He stopped short of offering any specific price target tied to the finding.

"...As fiscal imbalances grow and investors reassess the long-term purchasing power of fiat currencies, Bitcoin can serve as a scarce, liquid alternative alongside gold. That combination of scarcity and differentiated return drivers can make Bitcoin a compelling addition to a modern diversified portfolio," Grayscale Head of Research said.

Follow us on X to get the latest news as it happens.

Bitcoin's Correlation Is Shifting Toward Gold. Source: Grayscale

The debasement trade refers to the argument that hard, supply-capped assets tend to appreciate as fiat currencies lose purchasing power over time.

That framing has gained traction as US federal debt has passed $40 trillion, with persistent fiscal deficits renewing attention on scarce alternatives to cash.

Why the Gold Correlation Shift Matters

Gold has already been on an extended bull run this year, reinforcing the narrative that investors are rotating toward traditional hedges against currency weakness.

Bitcoin's rising correlation with gold, rather than tech stocks, suggests at least part of that flow may now be extending into digital assets as well. Pandl argued that Bitcoin and other scarce digital assets may be entering a more favorable market regime under these conditions.

Grayscale's broader research this year has repeatedly linked Bitcoin's price action to the debasement trade, including a January note that described the asset's disconnect from currency weakness amid regulatory uncertainty.

"...Unchecked government debt growth undermines the credibility of fiat currencies and drives investors to seek out alternative stores of value like physical gold and certain cryptocurrencies—in digital assets we think the so-called "debasement trade" will primarily benefit Bitcoin, Ethereum, and Zcash...," Pandl noted.

Bitcoin's 90-day correlation with gold climbed above 50%, up from near zero at the start of 2026, while its correlation with the Nasdaq 100 fell from above 60% to approximately 33%, according to a research note published by Grayscale on Aug 27.

Grayscale Head of Research Zach Pandl has noted that over the past year, amid the artificial intelligence investment boom, Bitcoin had been trading like a high-beta asset, meaning greater price volatility relative to the broader market, but recent signals suggest a shift in that dynamic.

Grayscale frames the shift as a rotation Pandl describes as the return of the "debasement trade", renewed investor focus on Bitcoin's scarcity, monetary independence, and role as a store of value. The 90-day figures are drawn from a rolling window and are backward-looking.

Related: Elon Musk's AI warning about the dollar is starting to come true

"The regime change comes as the macro backdrop is once again bringing the debasement trade into focus. U.S. federal debt recently crossed $40 trillion, while the long end of the Treasury curve has sold off meaningfully over the past year," Pandl wrote in his report.

The debt context

U.S. gross federal debt crossed $40 trillion on Aug 18, reaching approximately $40.05 trillion, according to Treasury Department data. The total reached about $40.10 trillion by Aug 25.

The Congressional Budget Office projects a $1.9 trillion federal deficit for fiscal 2026 and expects annual deficits to expand under current law as interest costs, mandatory spending and borrowing requirements increase.

The 90-day correlation between gold and Bitcoin now sits around 0.5, its second-highest level on record. Longer term, since 2010, the correlation between the two assets is close to zero.

Where both assets stand

Both assets are still below the all-time highs they set last year, gold by about 14% and Bitcoin by about 37%.

Bitcoin price at press time. Source: Decibel

According to Decibel, Bitcoin was trading at approximately $79,457 at the time of writing. Gold was near $4,613 per ounce, as per Fortune.

Pandl argued that persistent deficits and higher long-term yields could encourage investors to seek scarce assets outside the government bond market.

"Larger debt balances, persistent deficits, and higher long-term yields have renewed the search for assets that can help hedge against deteriorating fiscal and monetary fundamentals," he wrote.

title: Stock futures mixed as Kevin Warsh prepares Jackson Hole speech
detail:
Stock futures mixed as Kevin Warsh prepares Jackson Hole speech
Stock futures mixed as Kevin Warsh prepares Jackson Hole speech · Quartz · Michael Nagle / Bloomberg via Getty Images
Cris Tolomia
Fri, August 28, 2026 at 7:00 AM CDT 2 min read
^GSPC
^NDX
^DJI

U.S. stock futures pointed in different directions Friday as investors looked ahead to Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh's keynote address at the Kansas City Fed's annual economic symposium in Jackson Hole, Wyoming.

S&P 500 futures hovered just under the flatline, Nasdaq 100 futures slipped 0.3%, and Dow Jones Industrial Average futures nudged into positive territory. Warsh is scheduled to speak at 10 a.m. ET, according to The Wall Street Journal. According to CME's FedWatch tool, fed funds futures assign roughly a 64% chance that policymakers leave rates unchanged at their next gathering.

Warsh has been more tight-lipped than his predecessors, and traders are watching for any signals on the direction of interest rates, according to the Journal. Because Friday marks his first Jackson Hole keynote, investors are paying close attention to the language he uses. "New chairs use this stage to set the frame for their tenure, and whatever language he establishes Friday gets applied to every data print for the next year," Natalia Lojevsky, managing director at CIFC Asset Management, told CNBC.

Marvell Technology's roughly 8% premarket drop dragged chip stocks lower and put pressure on Nasdaq futures. Investors were let down by the company's outlook for non-GAAP gross margin in the current quarter, according to CNBC. Gap stock climbed 14% despite a mixed quarterly report after the retailer named a new chief executive for its Old Navy brand.

Thursday's session ended on a positive note, with Nvidia's post-earnings surge of nearly 9% doing much of the heavy lifting. It was also the strongest session since Aug. 4 for the technology sector, the S&P 500, and the Nasdaq Composite. With Thursday's gains, all three major indexes are on pace to end the week higher. Should the Dow finish in the green, it would snap a two-week losing streak for the blue-chip index.

Markets in the Asia-Pacific region closed mixed Friday. Japan's Nikkei 225 added 0.41%, Australia's S&P/ASX 200 gained 0.6%, South Korea's Kospi fell 1.79%, and China's CSI 300 dropped 0.46%. The dollar and Treasury yields showed little movement before Warsh took the stage, and Brent crude futures were changing hands near $88 a barrel.
